hook.title: Your commit messages are a *diary*. Write better ones.

scenes.before:
git commit -m "stuff"
git commit -m "fix"
git commit -m "more fixes"
scenes.after:
git commit -m "Fix login redirect after password reset"
git commit -m "Add rate limit to signup endpoint"
scenes.title: Your git log, *fixed*
One change per *commit*
scenes.body: Small commits are easy to review and easy to undo.

scenes.title: Say what it *does*
scenes.body: Start with a verb: Fix, Add, Remove. The log should read like a changelog.

end.title: Follow for more *code* tips
end.sub: follow for daily AI + code tips

caption:
"fix" and "stuff" are fine until you need to find which commit broke something.

Two rules:
1. One change per commit
2. Start the message with a verb and say what it does

Your git log turns into a changelog, and undoing one bad change stops being scary.

Send this to the person whose last commit says "fix".
